sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Stable expression confirmed in Panc1 cells; functional assays (invasion, migration) performed on the tagged line, but surface accessibility of the Flag tag itself was not reported in the ledger clips.
sites.rationale: SEMA5A is a type I single-pass TM protein with signal peptide residues 1–22 and mature ectodomain beginning at residue 23; the C-terminus (992–1074) is intracellular. Because exactly one terminus is extracellular, the topology_derived rule places the Flag tag after the SP cleavage site at residue 22, before the mature N-terminal glutamate (E23). Python confirmed residue 22 = P and residue 23 = E from the canonical sequence. The insert site is 948 residues from the TM boundary, satisfying all distance constraints. Full-length mouse Sema5A bearing a Flag epitope tag was cloned into pBK-CMV and stably transfected into Panc1 pancreatic cancer cells (PMC2888907). No residue is named in the clips; SEMA5A has exactly one extracellular terminus (N-terminus after SP cleavage at residue 22), so the position is derived from topology.

literature_notes: L1 and L2 are two clips from the same paper (PMC2888907) reporting the same construct; L1 is used as the primary supporting clip. Neither clip specifies which terminus carries the Flag tag, nor do they report surface staining or flow cytometry of the tag. The topology_derived rule applies because SEMA5A has exactly one extracellular terminus. Confidence is medium rather than high because the clips do not confirm the tag is extracellular (it could be a C-terminal intracellular Flag, a common alternative). No internal loop insertions are supported by the ledger. No residue-level position is named anywhere in the ledger, so no 'validated' site can be called.
